3.3 Chapter 2 Counterpoints and the Solutions Novel 
Feature Proposals 
This section seeks to explore the literature review within chapter two, and 
critically analyse various findings. This foundation of knowledge along with 
frameworks including microlearning, cognitive load theory and spaced repetition, 
provide much of the bedrock behind the justification of the proposed features. 
The structure of a lesson, with the incorporation of short-form content 
interweaved with questions, is a direction solution to cognitive load theory as 
discussed by (Sweller, 1988; Brame, 2016). This approach aims to break down 
content into digestible chunks, minimising extraneous load and optimising 
germane and intrinsic loads. This methodology is validated by the literature, that 
highlights that cognitive load should be managed (Sweller, 1988; Brame, 2016). 
With the noted drop in attention spans (Twenge & Campbell, 2018; Gausby, 
2015); an emphasis on microlearning, with lesson lengths around five minutes 
as proposed by (Barana, et al., 2019; Brame, 2016), poses to be an effective 
strategy. Smaller lesson sizes are additionally highly suited to spaced repetition 
due to their easily repeatable nature. A spaced repetition approach which 
dynamically adjusts revision intervals based on student performance, follows 
principles by (Toppino & Gerbier, 2014). Utilisation of spaced repetition offers a 
scientifically based strategy for long-term memory retention. 
The importance of performance-contingent rewards is emphasised by (Daniel, et 
al., 2015), highlighting their positive effects on motivation and student 
engagement. This may be achieved using a score and digital badges. Inspired by 
(Gabe & Christopher, n.d.) a competitive leader board rating students based on 
points earned will likely further motivative students. This strategy resonates with
